channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro flat lines near mid-1.1500s vs USD as traders await US CPI amid Iran uncertainty
item.description: The EUR/USD pair struggles to gain any meaningful traction and holds steady around the 1.1545-1.1550 area during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds ground ahead of RBA policy decision
item.description: AUD/USD regains ground after registering modest losses the previous day, trading around 0.7060 during Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair gains as the Australian Dollar (AUD) remains stronger ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) interest rate decision later in the day.

item.title: RBA set to hold interest rate as softer inflation shifts outlook
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is on track to keep the Official Cash Rate (OCR) steady at 4.35% for the second consecutive meeting on Tuesday.

item.title: Breaking: Gold rallies further beyond $4,400; highest since early June
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) scales higher for the third consecutive day – also marking the fifth day of a positive move in the previous six – and climbs to its highest level since June 5, further beyond the $4,400 mark during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds losses near $66.00 on Fed hike fears, oil surge
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) depreciates after two days of gains, trading around $66.00 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The price of non-yielding Silver has taken a hit recently as rising oil prices spark renewed inflation fears and heighten expectations for interest rate hikes.

item.title: United States Dollar Index consolidates below 100.00 as bulls await US CPI amid Iran risks
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, struggles to capitalize on the previous day's positive move and oscillates in a range during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7900 vs. 6.7884 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7900 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7884 and 6.7497 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI hovers around $81.50 as US-Iran peace talks stall
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price moves little after registering gains over 6.5% in the previous day, trading around $81.40 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Intervention bought the Japanese Yen a price, not a buyer
item.description: The Yen has surrendered close to a full percent through the session, with the pair up 0.93% and changing hands just above 159.00 after a 120-pip range running from the 158.00 handle to short of 159.50.

item.title: The Australian Dollar rallies without an Australian reason
item.description: The Australian Dollar has traded a band of barely 20 pips through the session, holding above 0.7050 and easing 0.15% inside it. That is the tightest daily range the pair has produced in weeks, and it arrives at the end of a run of close to 200 pips from the late-June trough just above 0.6850.

item.title: British Pound Sterling borrows its rally from American payrolls
item.description: Cable has spent the session inside a band of barely 45 pips straddling 1.3500, up 0.13% and holding its best ground since mid-July.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: 100-day SMA caps Euro recovery
item.description: The Euro is poised to end Monday’s session with losses of about 0.13% against the Greenback, as recent news points to a delay in talks between the US and Iran, while, from a technical perspective, EUR/USD stalled at the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) near 1.1568.

item.title: Fed's Hammack calls for rate hikes, says policy not restrictive enough
item.description: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack crossed the wires on Monday and was hawkish, noting that the current rate is not “meaningfully restricting the economy” and that there is a need for some number of rate hikes.

item.title: US Treasury yields climb as Oil spike revives CPI jitters
item.description: US Treasury yields rose on Monday as traders braced for the release of US inflation figures this week, following a worse-than-expected Nonfarm Payrolls report last Friday.

item.title: Citi Mexico Survey expects Banxico hold, USD/MXN ending 2026 at 17.90
item.description: Citi Mexico released the Expectations Survey on Monday, in which the central bank polled 35 economists to gather their forecasts for monetary policy, the USD/MXN exchange Rate, inflation expectations, and economic growth.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slips as firm US Dollar and Oil keep the Kiwi pinned
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) trades near 0.5900 against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, giving back a little ground after a run toward multi-day highs last week.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD extends rally and eyes $69
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price climbs over 3% on Monday even though US Treasury yields rose, with the white metal refreshing seven-week highs at $66.07. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades at $65.76 with buyers eyeing key resistance levels.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms as Oil surges on Hormuz
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) traded broadly firmer on Monday, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) up around 0.2% and holding just above 99.80 as Oil surged more than 6% on the ongoing Strait of Hormuz standoff.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average begins pricing a 2029 war premium
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 53,900 on Monday, lower by three tenths of a percent and pinned to the bottom of a session that has covered barely 200 points, the narrowest daily bar in weeks. Every price of the day sits inside Friday's range, and Friday's sat inside Thursday's.

item.title: China: Cost-driven reflation and narrow profit gains – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered analysts Carol Liao and Moriarty Lam argue that China’s reflation remains largely cost-driven, with industrial profit recovery concentrated in AI- and oil-related sectors. They highlight that domestic demand continues to lag supply, creating a persistent imbalance.

item.title: United States: Weak payrolls and softer retail sales – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes July payrolls surprised sharply to the downside, with headline jobs dragged by government hiring, while private employment stayed near breakeven.

item.title: Mexican Peso rally pauses ahead of US inflation report
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) loses some ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday as traders book profits after a worse-than-expected US jobs report last week and as eyes turn to the release of US inflation figures on Wednesday.

item.title: WTI jumps over 6% as Strait of Hormuz reopening remains uncertain
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) jumps more than 6% on Monday, erasing last week’s losses as uncertainty over when the Strait of Hormuz will reopen keeps supply concerns and the geopolitical risk premium firmly in place. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $81.15 per barrel, near a one-week high.

item.title: Breaking: Iran won't negotiate with the US until Trump's term is done
item.description: In a major setback to efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and cool Middle East tensions, Iran ruled out any future negotiations with United States (US) President Donald Trump, according to Iranian outlets and a X post by an adviser to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry window opens with caveats – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu and David Tam argue that a more dovish Federal Reserve (Fed) and weaker United States (US) labor data have improved conditions for Latin American (LatAm) carry trades, but broken correlations with commodities and lingering inflation risks limit momentum.

item.title: US President Trump says Iran should pay for regional damage
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump used a post on his Truth Social platform to push back on Iran's demands for war reparations, arguing that Tehran, not Washington, should carry the bill for the damage and lives lost across the region.

item.title: Gold edges higher as Hormuz delays, US CPI keep traders cautious
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price edges up at the beginning of the week as the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz faces delays due to demands from Iran to the US, and is capped by the modest strength of the Greenback, with traders eyeing the release of crucial US inflation data.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as surprise current account deficit weighs
item.description: USD/JPY advances 0.73% on Monday and trades around 158.95 at the time of writing.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar takes back two months in ten sessions
item.description: The Canadian Dollar trades at its strongest against the US Dollar since the second week of June, with the rate holding just above 1.3900 into the afternoon.

item.title: British Pound climbs as Hormuz talks stall, US CPI in focus
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances during the North American session on Monday, up 0.2% as markets digest developments in the Middle East and await crucial inflation data in the United States (US). The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3520 after bouncing off daily lows of 1.3483.
